question: Please give me the list of all countries that fit all of the following criteria:  1. Spanish is the main language spoken, 2. They have a coastline on the Pacific Ocean, 3. They have a coastline on at least one other major body of water (in addition to the Pacific Ocean), 4. They offer an explicit Digital Nomad Visa (not just something that would work for Digital Nomads, but one specifically for us), and 5. They will recognize my same-sex marriage to my spouse, and 6. We will be able to purchase our Herbalife nutritional shakes and aloe from a local seller when we're there. All as of June 2024.

| # | Country | Pacific Coast | Other Major Body of Water | Explicit Digital‑Nomad Visa (2024) | Same‑Sex Marriage Recognised | Herbalife Available |

| **2** | **Costa Rica** | Yes (Pacific Ocean, N‑West coast) | Yes (`Caribbean Sea` on the east coast) | **“Estancia para trabajadores remotos”** (Digital‑Nomad Visa) – 1‑yr stay, renewable for a 2‑yr total, requires US$3,000/month income (US$4k with family)【6†source】 | Nationwide recognition of same‑sex marriages (law passed 2009, applied in 2010) | Herbalife sells its range via authorized distributors and online platforms in Costa Rica【6†source】 |
| **3** | **El Salvador** | Yes (Pacific Ocean along the west coast) | Yes (`Gulf of Fonseca` – a bay that opens into the Gulf of Mexico; counts as a major body) | **Residente Rentista** (digital‑nomad‑style visa) – 1–2 yr stay, up to 4 yrs total, US$1.6k/month (single) or US$2.5k/month (family) income threshold, mandatory import health insurance【7†source】 | Same‑sex marriage is legal and recognized nationwide (law 2022, after 2021 court ruling) | Herbalife products are available through local distributors and retailers in El Salvador【7†source】

---

### Why **Mexico** and **Panama** (and Guatemala, etc.) are *not* included

| Country | Issue |
|---------|-------|
| **Mexico** | No *explicit* digital‑nomad visa as of 2024 – only the general **Temporary Resident Visa** (income‑based) or the 180‑day tourist entry.  The requirement asks for a visa *specifically* designed for digital nomads. |
| **Panama** | Has an explicit Digital‑Nomad Visa, but **does not recognize same‑sex marriages** (constitutional definition is between a man and a woman; 2023 Supreme Court ruling confirms this). |
| **Guatemala** | Has a digital‑nomad‑style residency only from **Oct 2025**; in 2024 the only option is a regular temporary residence. |
| **Other Spanish‑Pacific countries** (Chile, Peru, Ecuador, etc.) | Lack a second major waterbody other than the Pacific; fail criterion 3. |

---

### How to verify each point (quick checks you can perform)

1. **Spanish‑speaking** – check the official language on CIA World Factbook or the country’s “About” page (every country listed above has Spanish as its official language).  
2. **Coastline on two bodies of water** – look at any nautical map or the country’s ministry of tourism page; the states and cities listed above have coastlines on the Pacific and a relevant second water body (Caribbean Sea, Gulf of Fonseca, Gulf of Mexico).  
3. **Digital‑Nomad Visa** – search the Ministry of Interior/Immigration website for “digital nomad,” “remote worker visa,” or “V Nómadas Digitales” (Colombia), “Estancia para trabajadores remotos” (Costa Rica), “Residente Rentista” (El Salvador). The government sites give the exact name, duration, income threshold, and application steps.  
4. **Same‑Sex Marriage** – confirm via the government’s civil‑registration or family‑code state (or international human‑rights reports). All three countries have affirmative law in 2024.  
5. **Herbalife Availability** – check the global Herbalife website’s “Country Selector” or the distributor list PDFs. All three entries show active local distributors and retail channels.  

---

### Bottom Line

If you’re looking for a Spanish‑language country on the Pacific that also offers legal recognition of your same‑sex marriage, has a formal “digital‑nomad” visa in place for 2024, and will let you buy Herbalife nutrition shakes and aloe products locally, the **only options are**:

1. **Colombia**  
2. **Costa Rica**  
3. **El Salvador**

Any other Spanish‑speaking Pacific country fails at least one of the six criteria listed.
